nodes.label: Four coupling schemes price four routes to one object
nodes.rationale: A coupling scheme is a basis change and the atom does not move under it, so the four standard schemes must agree on the physics and may disagree only on bookkeeping. The 2.17-fold spread in cell counts prices four routes to one object, not four objects.

nodes.label: jK cell count of Lambda-13 = 199,130
nodes.rationale: Measured on the rebuilt tower at the caps of §7.4; LK rebuilt from its recoupling chain at 341,150, while LS and jj only bracket — [383,065, 597,325] containing 431,050 and [160,380, 244,060] containing 206,520 — because the looseness convention is named but not valued by the physics.

nodes.label: The exact J multiset is identical across all four coupling schemes
nodes.rationale: Computed independently through the jK, LS and jj chains the multiset agrees in 15 of 15 configurations tested, while the envelopes differ (64.4 per cent through K against 39.4 direct). The index remembers the route and the atom does not.

nodes.label: Mutual bound |2J - 2K| <= 1 privileges jK structurally
nodes.rationale: Because the outer electron's spin is a half, the final triangle degenerates to a mutual bound admissible on both sides, losing only the parity point 2J = 2K. The smallest quantum of angular momentum is the largest the constraint language can hold exactly, and the scheme reaching it is jK — the one high-n atoms realise because the weak coupling goes last.
